newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Burglars strike S.African deputy president's home.
newsitem.headline: Burglars strike S.African deputy president's home.

text.p: A top-level investigation has been launched into South Africa's VIP guard service after a break-in at Deputy President Thabo Mbeki's home in the heart of the government's ministerial estate, police said on Sunday.
"We definitely have to take a very serious look at them," a spokesman for the national police commissioner, Superintendent Leon Engelbrecht, told Reuters.
Guards are posted at the estate at all times, but burglars nevertheless stole a music system and camera which were kept in the study where the deputy president often works late at night.
He was away on official business when the theft was spotted on Wednesday this week. No forced entry was apparent.
The burglary prompted police minister Sydney Mufamadi to instruct the police commissioner, George Fivaz, to launch the shakeup of the VIP guard service.
It was the latest in a string of thefts from top government officials. Police officers have been charged with theft after goods were stolen from the houses of other cabinet ministers.

One member of the VIP unit arrested last month in connection with the thefts was found with duplicate keys to ministerial houses at his home. Police also recovered Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's gold wristwatch, prison minister Sipo Mzimela's leather jacket and Defence Minister Joe Modise's clock radio.
